key_insight: Deep learning PVS segmentation can look accurate on paper yet still fail to preserve the biological associations needed for valid Alzheimer’s research inference.
clinical_relevance: For AD biomarker studies, model selection should be based not only on Dice scores but also on whether the segmentations reproduce expected disease associations in the target cohort.
method: Benchmarked five open-source nnU-Net-based PVS segmentation models against manual labels
Tested performance in 60 multi-site ADNI-3 participants and 12 external VALDO scans
Compared overall, voxel, object, and lesion-wise Dice and checked biomarker association validity
evidence_signal: ADNI-PVS-Net had the best internal Dice (0.58±0.14) but dropped to ≤0.11 externally, while only AD-trained models reproduced the expected PVS-amyloid relationship.
watch_item: External generalizability and downstream biological validity can diverge, and some models misclassified substantial white matter hyperintensity as PVS.
paper_title: Examining the Clinical Utility of Deep Learning Models for Perivascular Space Segmentation in Alzheimer's Disease
